## Overview

> [!NOTE]
> This PR is an implementation suggestion for #61396. It shows one way to
> implement phase 2, so that reviewers can see the `ON_OVERWRITE` stores and
> the `lazy` policy in code. It is on top of #61426. The names, the config
> keys, the data structures in the connector, and the split into PRs can change
> after the RFC review. Please put comments on the design in the RFC, and
> comments on the code here.

Phase 2 of #61396, on top of #61426. The stack is six commits on top of
`29f69746b0`, the current tip of #61426; review the range
`29f69746b0..f75d71ffee`. The intermediate branches of the stack stay local,
so `git range-diff 29f69746b0..f75d71ffee` shows the six commits.

This PR adds lazy stores. With the new `lazy` store mode, the CPU stores a
chunk only when HBM is about to overwrite it, and not when the model computes
it. Then the CPU holds mainly the chunks that HBM lost, and not copies of the
chunks in HBM. So the total cache can come near the sum of HBM and CPU.

The default mode stays `eager`. With `eager`, the connector keeps no new
data, and the behavior is the same as on #61426.

```python
"kv_connector_extra_config": {"store_mode": "lazy"}
```

## Claims

- The manager selects its store triggers: `OffloadingManager.store_triggers`
  is an ordered tuple, `(ON_COMPUTE,)` by default. The CPU manager reads the
  new `store_mode` key. `lazy` gives `(ON_OVERWRITE,)`.
- `StoreHandlerFactory` replaces the `HANDLER_FOR_TRIGGER` dict of #61426: a
  class-level registry keyed by trigger, `register_handler(handler_cls)` which
  takes the key from `handler_cls.trigger`, and
  `create_handlers(config, manager_store_triggers, events_tracker,
  vllm_config, kv_cache_config, extra_config)`. The factory puts the layout
  handlers first, then one handler per trigger that the manager asks for, and
  refuses a trigger set that is empty or has duplicates.
- `check_support` gains the connector's `extra_config` and the events tracker
  that the handler will get, so a handler refuses a configuration from the
  object it will actually use.
- The new `OnOverwriteStoreHandler` sends `ON_OVERWRITE` stores, with
  `req_context=None`. It stores a chunk in the step in which core gives a block
  of the chunk to a new owner that does not expect the chunk data there. The
  store completes before the forward pass of the step.
- The handler keeps an overwrite map, from GPU block to the chunks in HBM on
  that block. A chunk enters the map when the model computes it, and when a
  load from the CPU completes; a load that fails contributes nothing. A
  request that starts again from token 0 records its chunks again.
- A prefix hit is not an overwrite. The handler compares the expected key of
  each block in the step, from `req.block_hashes`, with the block key in the
  map. A block copy, and a block of a group that is not offloaded, expect new
  data.
- Sliding window groups and preempted requests work in lazy mode. The new
  `first_live_chunk_idx` hook gives the first chunk of a group whose block ids
  the handler may still read, so the scheduler zeroes stale sliding-window
  block ids only past it.
- New handler hooks: blocks allocated to a request, the blocks allocated in a
  step (a read-only snapshot), load complete, and the first live chunk. The
  scheduler keeps only the set of blocks allocated in the step.
- The cache policy hooks take `req_context=None` for a store after the
  request finishes: `insert` and `on_store_miss`. The LRU policy orders a
  chunk by the key positions of its request; without a request, it uses the
  plain recency rank. ARC does not read the context.
- New checks at start, in `OnOverwriteStoreHandler.check_support`:
  - `self_describing_kv_events`: the payload is built from the request that
    stored the chunk, and an `ON_OVERWRITE` store has no request.
  - The V2 model runner, if the KV cache needs zeroing (a KV cache with more
    than one dtype): V2 zeroes a reused block, and applies the CoW copies,
    before the store reads it.
- Mamba `align` groups are not a refusal. `select_store_candidates` skips a
  CoW-source group, and the scheduler adds the `ON_HANDOFF` handler of #61426
  for a mamba-align layout, which stores that group. On V2 such a layout needs
  KV cache zeroing, so the check above refuses it there.
- The CPU manager refuses `ON_OVERWRITE` with a `store_threshold` of 2 or
  more. The tiering spec accepts only `eager`.
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md` documents `store_mode`, including the
  V2 restriction.

## Validation

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The numbers in this section are **old**. They were measured on the tree
> before the stack was rebased onto the current tip of #61426 (`29f69746b0`);
> at that time the base was the old PR1 commit `165972849a`. Re-run them before
> this PR leaves draft.

Old commands, on the old tree:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py
pre-commit run --from-ref main --to-ref HEAD
```

Old result: with `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/` in full,
1421 passed, 5 skipped; #61426 gave 1382 passed, 5 skipped on the same files.
The six `test_cache_reset_*` tests need `/dev/shm` and failed on that macOS
host on both trees. All pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy. Each commit
passed the same tests on its own (1413 to 1421 passed).

Fresh, on the rebased stack (`f75d71ffee`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_store_handler_factory.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py
```

614 passed, 6 failed. The six are `test_cache_reset_*`; they fail the same way
on `29f69746b0` itself on this macOS host. `pre-commit run --files` (ruff
check, ruff format, mypy) passes on every file in the stack diff.

The new tests cover:

- A lazy store after the request finishes, with `req_context=None` and
  `trigger=ON_OVERWRITE` at `prepare_store` and at `complete_store`.
- A prefix hit is not an overwrite, with and without async scheduling.
- Shared blocks, two chunks with the same key, chunks with null blocks, copy
  targets, and blocks of groups that the connector does not offload.
- A load target that holds a chunk: the store completes before the load.
- The loaded chunks get an `ON_OVERWRITE` offer when HBM loses them, and a
  load that fails adds no chunk.
- A request that starts again from token 0 records its chunks again.
- The handlers `{ON_COMPUTE}`, `{ON_OVERWRITE}`, and both, in each order, make
  the same offers.
- The handler factory: the layout handler comes first, an overlap between the
  layout and the manager raises, and `check_support` runs once per class, with
  the tracker that the handler will get.
- The `lazy` mode in the CPU manager, a key that both triggers offer, ARC
  ghost hits, and the start checks, also the V2 check with a mixed-dtype KV
  cache on both runners.

A local data simulator, not in this PR, runs a real scheduler and records the
data in each GPU block. It checks that each store reads the correct data, and
that lazy mode loses no chunk. Old result, pre-rebase: no errors in `eager`
and `lazy` mode, with and without async scheduling, with sliding window groups,
preemptions, and aborts, for seeds 0-19.

Evals: also measured on the old tree, before the rebase.

| Eval | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `lazy` against `eager`, same CPU size: CPU hit rate, TTFT, throughput. See the two tables below. | Both modes give a clear gain on the overflow workload, and the two are close on the multiturn workload. |
| The wait before the forward pass: step time with `lazy` against `eager` | Inside the TPOT numbers below: lazy adds 1.3 ms per output token on multiturn (+6.2%) and removes 7.7 ms on overflow, because it gets more CPU hits. There is no separate measurement. |

Setup: Qwen3-8B, TP=1, one H100, `--max-model-len 16384`,
`--num-gpu-blocks-override 4096`, CPU tier 10 GiB, `eviction_policy lru`. One source
tree (`lazy` tip) and one image. Only `kv_connector_extra_config` changes between the
two modes: `store_mode` absent for `eager`, `"store_mode": "lazy"` for `lazy`. One run
per cell, seed 0.

Overflow workload: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition`, 48 prefixes of
4096 tokens, 768 prompts, concurrency 32, suffix 32, output 64.

| Metric | `eager` | `lazy` | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU hit rate (external hits / queries) | 6.8% | 24.0% | +17.2 pp |
| Loads from CPU | 31.6 GB | 112.0 GB | +254% |
| Stores to CPU | 308.2 GB | 258.6 GB | -16.1% |
| Mean TTFT | 1367 ms | 1211 ms | -11.5% |
| P99 TTFT | 2340 ms | 2528 ms | +8.0% |
| Request throughput | 12.92 req/s | 14.34 req/s | +11.0% |
| Token throughput | 53490 tok/s | 59360 tok/s | +11.0% |
| Mean TPOT | 44.27 ms | 36.55 ms | -17.4% |

Multiturn workload: `benchmark_serving_multi_turn.py`, 48 conversations, 16 clients,
6 to 10 turns each, common prefix 500 tokens, prefix about 3000 tokens.

| Metric | `eager` | `lazy` | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU hit rate | 0.0% | 0.15% | +0.15 pp |
| Stores to CPU | 151.8 GB | 138.8 GB | -8.6% |
| Request throughput | 6.73 req/s | 6.42 req/s | -4.5% |
| Mean TTFT | 255 ms | 234 ms | -8.1% |
| Mean TPOT | 21.26 ms | 22.57 ms | +6.2% |
| Duplicate blocks (mean) | 3317 | 7 | -99.8% |

The two runs gave 296 and 290 responses in a fixed 44 s window, so the throughput
difference on that workload is within run noise. A duplicate block is one KV block that
two requests hold in the same tier, so `lazy` removes the cross-request copies that
`eager` keeps. This agrees with the earlier Falcon runs.

## Details

- **Why the connector keeps a map.** When core gives a block to a new owner,
  the connector sees only the block id. The old request can be gone, and the
  block pool removes the block hash at that time. So the connector records the
  key and the blocks of each chunk at its offer. The manager keeps no GPU
  data, as today.
- **Why `req_context=None`.** A lazy store can come after
  `on_request_finished`. A late `on_request_finished` or a dummy request makes
  the manager and each tier keep the request state while HBM holds any block of
  the request.
- **Why the V2 check.** The V2 model runner zeroes new blocks and applies the
  CoW copies in `update_requests`, before `handle_preemptions` flushes the
  `ON_OVERWRITE` stores. Thus such a store can read zeroed or copied data, and
  save it under a valid key. No connector hook runs earlier on V2, so the
  handler refuses KV cache zeroing. The V1 runner flushes first.
- **CoW copies on V2 are not refused.** CoW copies are not only for Mamba.
  `SingleTypeKVCacheManager` also copies a block at a partial local prefix
  hit: with `prefix_match_unit` smaller than the block size, or with KV cache
  groups of different block sizes. On V2, such a copy runs before the
  `ON_OVERWRITE` store. I read this in the code; no test or run shows it. This
  PR does not refuse it. Use `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` for these setups.
- **Mamba `align` layouts.** The lazy handler does not store a CoW-source
  group: `select_store_candidates` skips it. #61426 adds the `ON_HANDOFF`
  handler for such a layout, and that handler stores the group when the
  scheduler hands the boundary block off, so a hybrid layout works in lazy
  mode on the V1 runner. On V2 a mamba layout needs KV cache zeroing
  (`KVCacheConfig.needs_kv_cache_zeroing`), so the zeroing check refuses lazy
  there. A fix outside the connector would be for V2 to call
  `handle_preemptions` before `update_requests`, as V1 does.
- **Known limits.**
  - Each lazy store completes before the forward pass, so the step waits.
  - With more than one KV cache group, the groups of one chunk leave HBM at
    different times. The chunk can give no hit for a short time. This costs hit
    rate only.
  - The partial last chunk is not stored. This is also true for EAGLE and
    MTP models, which store their complete chunks with the same rule as
    `eager`.
  - No self-describing KV events (see the start checks).
  - No KV cache zeroing on the V2 model runner. Use
    `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`.
  - No tiering. The secondary tier API needs a `ReqContext`.
- **Not a duplicate.** Re-checked on 2026-11-04 with the `gh` searches of
  `AGENTS.md`. The only open PR that mentions #61396 is #64286, the predecessor
  of this one. The lazy-mode work for the other connector is separate:
  `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` has a `lazy_offload` mode, and #44791, #64394 and
  #65237 change it. That connector stores the blocks of the GPU free queue
  before the loss; this PR changes the offloading connector and stores at the
  loss.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

    different times. The chunk can give no hit for a short time. This costs hit
    rate only.
  - The partial last chunk is not stored. This is also true for EAGLE and
    MTP models, which store their complete chunks with the same rule as
    `eager`.
  - No self-describing KV events (see the start checks).
  - No KV cache zeroing on the V2 model runner. Use
    `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`.
  - No tiering. The secondary tier API needs a `ReqContext`.
- **Not a duplicate.** Re-checked on 2026-11-04 with the `gh` searches of
  `AGENTS.md`. The only open PR that mentions #61396 is #64286, the predecessor
  of this one. The lazy-mode work for the other connector is separate:
  `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` has a `lazy_offload` mode, and #44791, #64394 and
  #65237 change it. That connector stores the blocks of the GPU free queue
  before the loss; this PR changes the offloading connector and stores at the
  loss.

+def _create_handlers(
+    kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
+    extra_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
+    vllm_config=None,
+) -> dict[StoreTrigger, StoreTriggerHandler]:
+    vllm_config = vllm_config or _make_vllm_config(extra_config=extra_config)
+    spec = MockOffloadingSpec(build_offloading_config(vllm_config, kv_cache_config))
+    config = SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec(spec, vllm_config, kv_cache_config)
+    events_tracker = OffloadingEventsTracker(
+        spec.kv_events_config,
+        {
+            group.group_idx: group.kv_event_group_spec
+            for group in config.kv_group_configs
+        },
+    )
+    return StoreHandlerFactory.create_handlers(
+        config,
+        spec.get_manager().store_triggers,
+        events_tracker,
+        vllm_config,
+        kv_cache_config,
+        spec.extra_config,
+    )
+
+
+def test_the_layout_handler_is_added_first():
+    """ON_HANDOFF runs before the handlers of the manager, when the layout
+    hands off state blocks."""
+    handlers = _create_handlers(_make_mamba_hybrid_kv_cache_config())
+
+    assert list(handlers) == [StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF, StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE]
+    assert isinstance(handlers[StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF], OnHandoffStoreHandler)
+    assert isinstance(handlers[StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE], OnComputeStoreHandler)
+
+
+def test_a_trigger_of_the_layout_and_of_the_manager_raises():
+    """test_unsupported_store_triggers_raise covers an empty set and a
+    repeated manager trigger; only a layout/manager overlap is left."""
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="unique and not empty"):
+        _create_handlers(
+            _make_mamba_hybrid_kv_cache_config(), {"store_triggers": ["ON_HANDOFF"]}
+        )
+
+
+def test_check_support_is_called_once_per_class(monkeypatch):
+    """A refusal is per handler class, before any handler is made."""
+    calls: list[tuple[type, object, object, object, object]] = []
+
+    def record(cls, vllm_config, kv_cache_config, extra_config, events_tracker):
+        calls.append((cls, vllm_config, kv_cache_config, extra_config, events_tracker))
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(OnHandoffStoreHandler, "check_support", classmethod(record))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(OnComputeStoreHandler, "check_support", classmethod(record))
+    kv_cache_config = _make_mamba_hybrid_kv_cache_config()
+    vllm_config = _make_vllm_config(extra_config={"key": "value"})
+
+    _create_handlers(kv_cache_config, {"key": "value"}, vllm_config)
+
+    assert [cls for cls, *_ in calls] == [OnHandoffStoreHandler, OnComputeStoreHandler]
+    trackers = set()
+    for _, seen_vllm_config, seen_kv_cache_config, seen_extra_config, tracker in calls:
+        assert seen_vllm_config is vllm_config
+        assert seen_kv_cache_config is kv_cache_config
+        assert seen_extra_config == {"key": "value"}
+        assert isinstance(tracker, OffloadingEventsTracker)
+        trackers.add(id(tracker))
+    # Every class gets the same tracker, which is the one the handler will get.
+    assert len(trackers) == 1

+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.config import (
+    _group_kv_bytes_per_block,
+)

+    get_offloading_event_group_spec,
+)

+from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import eagle_proof_margin
+from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import SingleTypeKVCacheManager
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheSpec,
+    MambaSpec,
+    SlidingWindowSpec,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_spec_registry import KVCacheSpecRegistry
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import (

+    make_offload_key,

+logger = init_logger(__name__)

+class GroupOffloadConfig(NamedTuple):
+    group_idx: int
+    tokens_per_block: int
+    tokens_per_chunk: int
+    hashes_per_chunk: int
+    hashes_per_block: int
+    # KV cache spec metadata propagated onto emitted BlockStored events so
+    # KV-aware consumers can classify and filter the group.
+    kv_event_group_spec: OffloadingEventGroupSpec
+    # None below means full attention
+    sliding_window_size_in_chunks: int | None
+    kv_cache_spec: KVCacheSpec
+    # Cached manager class for this group's KV cache spec, resolved at init time
+    manager_cls: type[SingleTypeKVCacheManager]
+    # Partial-tail data for this group comes from the scheduler's CoW hand-off
+    # rather than the request block table.
+    requires_cow_source: bool = False
+    # True for EAGLE/MTP draft-model attention groups. Connectors using legacy
+    # hashes exclude their trailing chunk from store and load scheduling.
+    is_eagle_group: bool = False
+
+    def load_window_size_in_chunks(self, num_tokens: int) -> int | None:
+        window = self.sliding_window_size_in_chunks
+        if isinstance(self.kv_cache_spec, SlidingWindowSpec):
+            assert window is not None
+            # Lookup rounds the right edge up, but allocation retains the
+            # window ending at the actual hit boundary, possibly one chunk left.
+            right_padding = -num_tokens % self.tokens_per_chunk
+            window = max(
+                window,
+                cdiv(
+                    self.kv_cache_spec.sliding_window
+                    - 1
+                    + self.kv_cache_spec.extra_retained_tokens
+                    + right_padding,
+                    self.tokens_per_chunk,
+                ),
+            )
+        return window
+
+
+def resolve_mamba_align_size(
+    spec: "OffloadingSpec", kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig
+) -> int | None:
+    """Scan all KV cache groups in *spec* and return the single mamba alignment
+    size, or None if no group requires mamba alignment.
+
+    For MambaSpec groups in "align" cache mode the hit window must be
+    rounded down to a multiple of the offloaded chunk size. Asserts that all
+    such groups agree on the same value.
+    """
+    mamba_align_size: int | None = None
+    for group in spec.config.groups:
+        tokens_per_block = group.tokens_per_block
+        kv_spec = kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[group.group_id].kv_cache_spec
+        if isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec) and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align":
+            tokens_per_chunk = tokens_per_block * spec.blocks_per_chunk
+            assert mamba_align_size is None or mamba_align_size == tokens_per_chunk
+            mamba_align_size = tokens_per_chunk
+    return mamba_align_size
+
+
+class SchedulerOffloadConfig(NamedTuple):
+    kv_group_configs: tuple[GroupOffloadConfig, ...]
+    blocks_per_chunk: int
+    tokens_per_hash: int
+    num_workers: int
+    offload_prompt_only: bool
+    supports_partial_tail: bool
+    alignment_tokens: int | None = None
+    retention_interval: int | None = None
+    dcp_world_size: int = 1
+    sync_load_budget_bytes: int = 0
+    # KV bytes per token on one worker, summed over the offloaded groups.
+    kv_bytes_per_token: int = 0
+
+    # Per group, the tokens past a partial-tail boundary whose hash keys the
+    # group's partial-tail block. Non-zero only for EAGLE groups.
+    eagle_proof_margins: tuple[int, ...] = ()
+    # Lookahead block hashes already cover positions past the computed tokens.
+    num_hash_lookahead_tokens: int = 0
+
+    @property
+    def supports_handoff(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the KV cache manager can hand off state blocks."""
+        return any(cfg.requires_cow_source for cfg in self.kv_group_configs)
+
+    @property
+    def partial_tail_block_size(self) -> int:
+        if not self.supports_partial_tail:
+            return 0
+        return self.kv_group_configs[0].tokens_per_block
+
+    @property
+    def max_eagle_proof_margin(self) -> int:
+        return max(self.eagle_proof_margins, default=0)
+
+    def partial_tail_key_tokens(self, config_idx: int, boundary: int) -> int:
+        """Token position whose hash keys a group's partial-tail block."""
+        if not self.eagle_proof_margins:
+            return boundary
+        return boundary + self.eagle_proof_margins[config_idx]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_spec(
+        cls,
+        spec: OffloadingSpec,
+        vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+        kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
+    ) -> "SchedulerOffloadConfig":
+        # Determine the alignment token count from the full-attention group(s).
+        # This is the tokens_per_chunk of the full-attention group; load
+        # hits are always aligned to this boundary, so SWA blocks earlier in
+        # each segment can never serve a load hit. Relevant for hybrid
+        # architectures like DeepSeek V4 (MLA + SWA groups).
+        full_attn_tokens_per_chunk: set[int] = set()
+        for group in spec.config.groups:
+            if group.sliding_window_size_in_chunks is None:
+                full_attn_tokens_per_chunk.add(
+                    group.tokens_per_block * spec.blocks_per_chunk
+                )
+
+        # Only apply the optimization if there's a single consistent
+        # full-attention alignment size.  For pure SWA/Mamba models (no
+        # full-attention groups), fall back to the largest SWA/Mamba
+        # tokens_per_chunk so retention_interval has a boundary
+        # granularity to work with.
+        alignment_tokens: int | None = None
+        if len(full_attn_tokens_per_chunk) == 1:
+            alignment_tokens = full_attn_tokens_per_chunk.pop()
+        elif not full_attn_tokens_per_chunk:
+            all_tokens_per_chunk = [
+                tpb * spec.blocks_per_chunk for tpb in spec.tokens_per_block
+            ]
+            if all_tokens_per_chunk:
+                alignment_tokens = max(all_tokens_per_chunk)
+
+        retention_interval = vllm_config.cache_config.prefix_cache_retention_interval
+
+        eagle_groups = {
+            group.group_id
+            for group in spec.config.groups
+            if kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[group.group_id].is_eagle_group
+        }
+
+        use_eagle_block_drop = (
+            vllm_config.speculative_config is not None
+            and vllm_config.speculative_config.use_eagle_block_drop()
+        )
+        if use_eagle_block_drop and not eagle_groups:
+            # No group is annotated as holding drafter layers. This happens
+            # when the drafter owns no KV cache (e.g. KV-sharing drafters) or
+            # the model runner does not tag draft layers' KV cache specs.
+            # Treating every group as a drafter group here makes
+            # the volatile-tail pop apply to ALL groups, which can zero the
+            # whole request's offload hit whenever any group's servable
+            # window is a single chunk (issue #52735). Drafter KV served one
+            # chunk stale can only lower speculative acceptance rates — the
+            # target model verifies every draft — so fail toward serving.
+            logger.info_once(
+                "KV offloading: speculative decoding is enabled but no "
+                "KV-cache group is annotated as a drafter group; treating "
+                "all groups as non-draft for offloading."
+            )
+
+        if eagle_groups:
+            logger.info(
+                "KV offloading: EAGLE/MTP draft attention groups %s detected.",
+                sorted(eagle_groups),
+            )
+
+        kv_group_configs_list: list[GroupOffloadConfig] = []
+        for group in spec.config.groups:
+            group_id = group.group_id
+            tokens_per_block = group.tokens_per_block
+            kv_cache_group = kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[group_id]
+            kv_spec = kv_cache_group.kv_cache_spec
+            manager_cls = KVCacheSpecRegistry.get_manager_class(kv_spec)
+            assert manager_cls is not None, (
+                f"No manager found for KV cache spec {type(kv_spec).__name__}"
+            )
+            kv_group_configs_list.append(
+                GroupOffloadConfig(
+                    group_idx=group_id,
+                    tokens_per_block=tokens_per_block,
+                    tokens_per_chunk=tokens_per_block * spec.blocks_per_chunk,
+                    hashes_per_chunk=(
+                        (tokens_per_block * spec.blocks_per_chunk)
+                        // spec.tokens_per_hash
+                    ),
+                    hashes_per_block=tokens_per_block // spec.tokens_per_hash,
+                    sliding_window_size_in_chunks=group.sliding_window_size_in_chunks,
+                    kv_cache_spec=kv_spec,
+                    manager_cls=manager_cls,
+                    kv_event_group_spec=get_offloading_event_group_spec(kv_cache_group),
+                    is_eagle_group=group_id in eagle_groups,
+                    requires_cow_source=(
+                        isinstance(kv_spec, MambaSpec)
+                        and kv_spec.mamba_cache_mode == "align"
+                    ),
+                )
+            )
+        kv_group_configs = tuple(kv_group_configs_list)
+        group_block_sizes = {config.tokens_per_block for config in kv_group_configs}
+        has_partial_recurrent_group = any(
+            config.requires_cow_source
+            and config.tokens_per_block > spec.tokens_per_hash
+            for config in kv_group_configs
+        )
+        # Partial tails currently require one physical block per offload chunk
+        # and uniform, non-windowed groups so one boundary identifies every
+        # group's source. EAGLE groups key their partial tail at a proof
+        # position past the boundary. DCP needs additional hand-off semantics.
+        supports_partial_tail = (
+            spec.blocks_per_chunk == 1
+            and len(group_block_sizes) == 1
+            and has_partial_recurrent_group
+            and all(
+                config.sliding_window_size_in_chunks is None
+                or config.requires_cow_source
+                for config in kv_group_configs
+            )
+            and vllm_config.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size == 1
+        )
+
+        # Core's prefix cache matches an EAGLE group this many tokens past a
+        # hit and then drops them. A partial tail stores and looks up EAGLE
+        # groups at that proof position, with the margin rule of the core
+        # coordinator. Lookahead block hashes already key that position, so
+        # the groups need no margin.
+        eagle_proof_margins: tuple[int, ...] = ()
+        if supports_partial_tail and vllm_config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens == 0:
+            partial_tail_block_size = kv_group_configs[0].tokens_per_block
+            alignment = kv_cache_config.cache_hit_alignment_tokens
+            partial_hash_hits = (
+                alignment is not None and alignment < partial_tail_block_size
+            )
+            eagle_proof_margins = tuple(
+                eagle_proof_margin(
+                    partial_tail_block_size,
+                    spec.tokens_per_hash,
+                    partial_hash_hits
+                    and config.manager_cls.supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup,
+                )
+                if config.is_eagle_group and not config.requires_cow_source
+                else 0
+                for config in kv_group_configs
+            )
+
+        if retention_interval is not None:
+            if retention_interval < 0:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"prefix_cache_retention_interval "
+                    f"({retention_interval}) must be non-negative."
+                )
+            for config in kv_group_configs:
+                if (
+                    config.sliding_window_size_in_chunks is not None
+                    and retention_interval % config.tokens_per_chunk != 0
+                ):
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        f"prefix_cache_retention_interval "
+                        f"({retention_interval}) must be a multiple of "
+                        f"tokens_per_chunk ({config.tokens_per_chunk})."
+                    )
+
+        return cls(
+            num_workers=vllm_config.parallel_config.world_size,
+            kv_group_configs=kv_group_configs,
+            blocks_per_chunk=spec.blocks_per_chunk,
+            tokens_per_hash=spec.tokens_per_hash,
+            offload_prompt_only=spec.offload_prompt_only,
+            supports_partial_tail=supports_partial_tail,
+            alignment_tokens=alignment_tokens,
+            retention_interval=retention_interval,
+            dcp_world_size=vllm_config.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size,
+            # Per-step KV bytes (per worker) loaded within the step (0 disables).
+            sync_load_budget_bytes=int(
+                spec.extra_config.get("sync_load_budget_bytes", 0)
+            ),
+            kv_bytes_per_token=sum(
+                _group_kv_bytes_per_block(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[g.group_id])
+                // g.tokens_per_block
+                for g in spec.config.groups
+            ),
+            eagle_proof_margins=eagle_proof_margins,
+            num_hash_lookahead_tokens=vllm_config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens,
+        )
+

+@dataclass
+class RequestGroupState:
+    offload_keys: list[OffloadKey] = field(default_factory=list)
+    block_ids: list[int] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # Number of offloaded chunks hit (including GPU prefix cache)
+    # when the request first started
+    num_hit_chunks: int = 0
+    # End (exclusive) of the chunks that the current complete-chunk lookup
+    # confirmed as ready hits, including a popped EAGLE chunk.
+    lookup_hit_end_chunk_idx: int = 0
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class RequestOffloadState:
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig
+    req: Request
+    req_context: ReqContext
+    offloading_context: RequestOffloadingContext
+    group_states: tuple[RequestGroupState, ...] = field(init=False)
+    # upper bound on tokens to load for this request; None means no cap
+    max_load_tokens: int | None = None
+    # upper bound on tokens to offload for this request; None means no cap
+    max_offload_tokens: int | None = None
+    # number of hits in the GPU cache
+    num_locally_computed_tokens: int = 0
+    # In-flight job IDs. Per the connector's invariant, at any given time
+    # this contains either a single load job, or one or more store jobs.
+    transfer_jobs: set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
+    # time.monotonic() of this request's first deferred offload lookup;
+    # None once consumed (observed) or while no lookup is pending.
+    deferred_lookup_start_time: float | None = None
+    # Fine-grained token boundary selected beyond the last complete offload
+    # chunk. It is consumed when the corresponding load is scheduled.
+    partial_tail_boundary: int | None = None
+    # True once a load from the offload tier was scheduled for this request.
+    loaded_from_offload: bool = False
+    # Loaded attention keys cover their token positions. Recurrent state
+    # supports the whole reused external prefix.
+    load_key_ranges: list[tuple[int, int, OffloadKey]] = field(default_factory=list)
+    # True once on_request_finished has been signaled to the manager.
+    finished_signaled: bool = False
+    # A load for this request failed; all its later lookups, including after
+    # preemption, skip the offloaded cache so a faulting load is not retried.
+    load_failed: bool = False
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        self.group_states = tuple(
+            RequestGroupState() for _ in self.config.kv_group_configs
+        )
+        params = self.req.kv_transfer_params
+
+        # NOTE: This field is experimental and subject to change in the future.
+        raw = params.get("max_load_tokens") if params else None
+        if type(raw) is int and raw >= 0:
+            self.max_load_tokens = raw
+            logger.debug(
+                "Request %s: max_load_tokens set to %d",
+                self.req.request_id,
+                raw,
+            )
+        elif raw is not None:
+            logger.warning(
+                "max_load_tokens must be a non-negative int, got %r; ignoring", raw
+            )
+
+        # NOTE: This field is experimental and subject to change in the future.
+        raw = params.get("max_offload_tokens") if params else None
+        if type(raw) is int and raw >= 0:
+            self.max_offload_tokens = raw
+            logger.debug(
+                "Request %s: max_offload_tokens set to %d",
+                self.req.request_id,
+                raw,
+            )
+        elif raw is not None:
+            logger.warning(
+                "max_offload_tokens must be a non-negative int, got %r; ignoring", raw
+            )
+
+    def update_offload_keys(self) -> None:
+        for group_config, group_state in zip(
+            self.config.kv_group_configs, self.group_states
+        ):
+            stride = group_config.hashes_per_chunk
+            start = stride * (len(group_state.offload_keys) + 1) - 1
+            for req_block_hash in self.req.block_hashes[start::stride]:
+                key = make_offload_key(req_block_hash, group_config.group_idx)
+                group_state.offload_keys.append(key)
+                self.req_context.set_offload_key_position(
+                    key,
+                    len(group_state.offload_keys) * group_config.tokens_per_chunk,
+                )
+
+    def update_block_id_groups(
+        self, new_block_id_groups: tuple[list[int], ...] | None
+    ) -> None:
+        if new_block_id_groups is None:
+            return
+
+        for group_config, group_state in zip(
+            self.config.kv_group_configs, self.group_states
+        ):
+            group_state.block_ids.extend(new_block_id_groups[group_config.group_idx])
+
+    def storable_chunks(
+        self,
+        group_config: "GroupOffloadConfig",
+        group_state: RequestGroupState,
+        num_offloadable_tokens: int,
+        apply_eagle_drop: bool,
+    ) -> int:
+        """Number of allocated and keyed leading chunks eligible for store.
+
+        With legacy hashes, the volatile trailing chunk of an EAGLE/MTP group
+        is excluded while decoding: the draft-layer KV of the last accepted
+        position may be rewritten after spec-token rejection. During prefill
+        the trailing chunk is stable (the draft input for a chunk's last
+        position is the next prompt token), so it is stored immediately.
+        Once the request has finished, no further spec-token rejection can
+        rewrite the tail, so the exclusion is lifted and the final chunk
+        becomes storable (issue #52735). The exclusion must be applied
+        consistently everywhere the ON_COMPUTE progress is derived:
+        otherwise the trailing chunk of each step is skipped on collection but
+        jumped over by the progress, so it is never re-considered
+        and a permanent hole breaks prefix-reuse lookup. ``is_finished`` is
+        monotonic, so the finish-time calls all see the lifted exclusion.
+        """
+        num_chunks = num_offloadable_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_chunk
+        is_decoding = num_offloadable_tokens > self.req.num_prompt_tokens
+        # Finished requests have no pending speculation.
+        if (
+            apply_eagle_drop
+            and group_config.is_eagle_group
+            and is_decoding
+            and not self.req.is_finished()
+        ):
+            num_chunks = max(0, num_chunks - 1)
+        num_allocated_chunks = (
+            len(group_state.block_ids) // self.config.blocks_per_chunk
+        )
+        num_keyed_chunks = len(group_state.offload_keys)
+        return min(num_chunks, num_allocated_chunks, num_keyed_chunks)
+
+    def num_offloadable_tokens(self, num_computed_tokens: int) -> int:
+        num = min(num_computed_tokens, self.req.num_tokens)
+        if self.config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens:
+            num = min(
+                num,
+                len(self.req.block_hashes) * self.config.tokens_per_hash,
+            )
+        if self.max_offload_tokens is not None:
+            num = min(num, self.max_offload_tokens)
+        if self.config.offload_prompt_only:
+            num = min(num, self.req.num_prompt_tokens)
+        return num
+
+    def register_boundary_key(self, group_idx: int, boundary_tokens: int) -> OffloadKey:
+        hash_idx = boundary_tokens // self.config.tokens_per_hash - 1
+        key = make_offload_key(self.req.block_hashes[hash_idx], group_idx)
+        self.req_context.set_offload_key_position(key, boundary_tokens)
+        return key
+
+    def update_num_hit_chunks(self, num_cached_tokens: int) -> None:
+        for group_config, group_state in zip(
+            self.config.kv_group_configs, self.group_states
+        ):
+            group_state.num_hit_chunks = (
+                num_cached_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_chunk
+            )

+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import replace
+from typing import NamedTuple

+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.state import (
+    GroupOffloadConfig,
+    RequestOffloadState,
+    SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+)
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import SchedulerOutput

+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import OffloadKey, make_offload_key
+from vllm.v1.request import Request, RequestStatus
+
+
+class StoreCandidates(NamedTuple):
+    """The computed chunks of a request that a trigger can store."""
+
+    num_offloadable_tokens: int
+    keys: list[OffloadKey]
+    # (config_idx, chunk_idx) of each key
+    chunk_positions: list[tuple[int, int]]
+    # (start_chunk_idx, end_chunk_idx) of each group
+    group_ranges: list[tuple[int, int]]
+
+
+def select_store_candidates(
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+    scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+    req_status: RequestOffloadState,
+    start_chunk_idxs: Sequence[int],
+) -> StoreCandidates:
+    """Select the computed chunks of a request, from the given chunk of each group.
+
+    Args:
+        config: the scheduler offloading config.
+        scheduler_output: the output of the current scheduler step.
+        req_status: the request.
+        start_chunk_idxs: for each group, the first chunk that the trigger did
+            not store yet.
+
+    Returns:
+        The keys and positions of the reachable chunks, and the chunk range of
+        each group.
+
+    """
+    blocks_per_chunk = config.blocks_per_chunk
+    req = req_status.req
+
+    if req.status is RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED:
+        num_tokens_after_batch = req.num_computed_tokens
+    elif req.is_finished():
+        # Clamp to the GPU prefix cache's commit point. The final sampled
+        # token's slot is never committed (under spec decode it holds a
+        # rejected draft's KV), so a block ending there must not be stored.
+        # A request that finished before its prefill completed (e.g. an
+        # error) has computed only num_computed_tokens of its prompt.
+        num_tokens_after_batch = min(
+            req.num_computed_tokens,
+            max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1),
+        )
+    else:
+        num_scheduled_tokens = scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens[req.request_id]
+        num_tokens_after_batch = req.num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens
+
+    num_offloadable_tokens = req_status.num_offloadable_tokens(num_tokens_after_batch)
+    prompt_offloadable_tokens = req_status.num_offloadable_tokens(req.num_prompt_tokens)
+
+    # Filter out chunks skipped due to sliding window attention / SSM
+    # or unreachable by the load path's alignment constraints.
+    new_offload_keys: list[OffloadKey] = []
+    chunk_positions: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
+    group_store_ranges: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
+
+    apply_eagle_drop = not config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens
+    reachable_boundaries: tuple[int, ...] = ()
+    if config.retention_interval is not None:
+        reachable_boundaries = (req.num_prompt_tokens - 1,)
+        if req.shared_prefix_boundary:
+            reachable_boundaries += (req.shared_prefix_boundary,)
+
+    for config_idx, (group_config, group_state, stored_chunk_idx) in enumerate(
+        zip(config.kv_group_configs, req_status.group_states, start_chunk_idxs)
+    ):
+        num_chunks = req_status.storable_chunks(
+            group_config, group_state, num_offloadable_tokens, apply_eagle_drop
+        )
+
+        start_chunk_idx = stored_chunk_idx
+        prompt_horizon_chunks = (
+            prompt_offloadable_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_chunk
+        )
+        final_swa_alignment_blocks = _final_swa_alignment_blocks(config, group_config)
+        reconsider_final_swa_tail = (
+            req.is_finished()
+            and num_chunks != prompt_horizon_chunks
+            and config.retention_interval is None
+            and final_swa_alignment_blocks is not None
+        )
+        if config.retention_interval is not None or group_config.is_eagle_group:
+            store_horizon_chunks = None
+        elif req.is_finished():
+            store_horizon_chunks = num_chunks
+        elif num_chunks <= prompt_horizon_chunks:
+            store_horizon_chunks = prompt_horizon_chunks
+        else:
+            # An active decode frontier is not a final request
+            # boundary. Only fixed alignment tails are reachable.
+            store_horizon_chunks = None
+        if reconsider_final_swa_tail:
+            assert final_swa_alignment_blocks is not None
+            horizon_blocks = num_chunks * blocks_per_chunk
+            partial_segment_start_block = (
+                horizon_blocks - horizon_blocks % final_swa_alignment_blocks
+            )
+            partial_segment_start_chunk = (
+                partial_segment_start_block // blocks_per_chunk
+            )
+            start_chunk_idx = min(start_chunk_idx, partial_segment_start_chunk)
+        group_store_ranges.append((start_chunk_idx, num_chunks))
+
+        if group_config.requires_cow_source:
+            continue
+
+        if num_chunks <= start_chunk_idx:
+            continue
+        offload_keys = group_state.offload_keys[start_chunk_idx:num_chunks]
+        # For each chunk, take the last corresponding GPU block. For
+        # blocks_per_chunk=3 and GPU block IDs 1 5 6 7 2 4 9 3 8,
+        # this selects GPU blocks 6 4 8.
+        # A block_id of 0 means either a sliding window / SSM skip
+        # or a stale entry that was zeroed out — skip it either way.
+        offload_block_ids = group_state.block_ids[
+            start_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk + blocks_per_chunk - 1 : num_chunks
+            * blocks_per_chunk : blocks_per_chunk
+        ]
+        assert len(offload_keys) == len(offload_block_ids)
+
+        # Use reachable_block_mask to filter unreachable chunks
+        # (SWA/Mamba sparsity + retention interval).
+        # reachable_block_mask operates in KV-block coordinates,
+        # so convert chunk indices to block indices.
+        block_mask = _reachable_store_block_mask(
+            config=config,
+            group_config=group_config,
+            start_chunk_idx=start_chunk_idx,
+            end_chunk_idx=num_chunks,
+            final_segment_end_chunk_idx=store_horizon_chunks,
+            reachable_boundaries=reachable_boundaries,
+        )
+
+        prompt_horizon_block_mask: list[bool] | None = None
+        if reconsider_final_swa_tail:
+            prompt_horizon_block_mask = _reachable_store_block_mask(
+                config=config,
+                group_config=group_config,
+                start_chunk_idx=start_chunk_idx,
+                end_chunk_idx=num_chunks,
+                final_segment_end_chunk_idx=prompt_horizon_chunks,
+                reachable_boundaries=reachable_boundaries,
+            )
+
+        for key_idx, (offload_key, block_id) in enumerate(
+            zip(offload_keys, offload_block_ids)
+        ):
+            if block_id == 0:
+                continue
+            abs_chunk_idx = start_chunk_idx + key_idx
+            if (
+                reconsider_final_swa_tail
+                and abs_chunk_idx < stored_chunk_idx
+                and (
+                    prompt_horizon_block_mask is None
+                    or any(
+                        prompt_horizon_block_mask[
+                            key_idx * blocks_per_chunk + block_idx
+                        ]
+                        for block_idx in range(blocks_per_chunk)
+                    )
+                )
+            ):
+                continue
+            # A chunk is reachable if any of its constituent
+            # blocks is reachable.
+            if block_mask is not None and not any(
+                block_mask[key_idx * blocks_per_chunk + b]
+                for b in range(blocks_per_chunk)
+            ):
+                continue
+            # A reachable null block would leave part of the chunk unwritten.
+            chunk_start = abs_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk
+            if any(
+                group_state.block_ids[chunk_start + b] == 0
+                and (block_mask is None or block_mask[key_idx * blocks_per_chunk + b])
+                for b in range(blocks_per_chunk)
+            ):
+                continue
+            new_offload_keys.append(offload_key)
+            chunk_positions.append((config_idx, abs_chunk_idx))
+
+    return StoreCandidates(
+        num_offloadable_tokens, new_offload_keys, chunk_positions, group_store_ranges
+    )
+
+
+def block_key(
+    req: Request, group_config: GroupOffloadConfig, block_idx: int
+) -> OffloadKey:
+    """The key of the data in one GPU block of a request."""
+    hash_idx = (block_idx + 1) * group_config.hashes_per_block - 1
+    return make_offload_key(req.block_hashes[hash_idx], group_config.group_idx)
+
+
+def _reachable_store_block_mask(
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+    group_config: GroupOffloadConfig,
+    start_chunk_idx: int,
+    end_chunk_idx: int,
+    final_segment_end_chunk_idx: int | None,
+    reachable_boundaries: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> list[bool] | None:
+    """Build the block mask for a range of candidate offload chunks."""
+    blocks_per_chunk = config.blocks_per_chunk
+    kv_cache_spec = group_config.kv_cache_spec
+    if isinstance(kv_cache_spec, SlidingWindowSpec) and (
+        kv_cache_spec.extra_retained_tokens
+    ):
+        # Offload restores all allocated history, including MTP re-prefill
+        # tokens. Widen only the store mask, not the model's attention window.
+        kv_cache_spec = replace(
+            kv_cache_spec,
+            sliding_window=(
+                kv_cache_spec.sliding_window + kv_cache_spec.extra_retained_tokens
+            ),
+            extra_retained_tokens=0,
+        )
+    return group_config.manager_cls.reachable_block_mask(
+        start_block=start_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk,
+        end_block=end_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk,
+        alignment_tokens=config.alignment_tokens,
+        kv_cache_spec=kv_cache_spec,
+        use_eagle=group_config.is_eagle_group,
+        retention_interval=config.retention_interval,
+        reachable_boundaries=reachable_boundaries,
+        dcp_world_size=config.dcp_world_size,
+        final_segment_end_block=(
+            final_segment_end_chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk
+            if final_segment_end_chunk_idx is not None
+            else None
+        ),
+    )
+
+
+def _final_swa_alignment_blocks(
+    config: SchedulerOffloadConfig, group_config: GroupOffloadConfig
+) -> int | None:
+    """Return representable final-tail alignment for a non-EAGLE SWA group."""
+    alignment_tokens = config.alignment_tokens
+    if (
+        alignment_tokens is None
+        or group_config.is_eagle_group
+        or not isinstance(group_config.kv_cache_spec, SlidingWindowSpec)
+        or alignment_tokens % group_config.tokens_per_block != 0
+    ):
+        return None
+    return alignment_tokens // group_config.tokens_per_block

+class StoreHandlerFactory:
+    """Registry of store handler classes, keyed by trigger.
+
+    Mirrors OffloadingSpecFactory and CachePolicyFactory: built-in handlers
+    are registered below, at import of this module, so a handler must be
+    registered before the scheduler builds its handlers. The scheduler names
+    no handler class.
+    """
+
+    _registry: dict[StoreTrigger, type[StoreTriggerHandler]] = {}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def register_handler(cls, handler_cls: type[StoreTriggerHandler]) -> None:
+        """Register a handler class for its trigger. Raise if registered twice."""
+        trigger = handler_cls.trigger
+        if trigger in cls._registry:
+            raise ValueError(f"Store trigger {trigger!r} is already registered.")
+        cls._registry[trigger] = handler_cls
+
+    @classmethod
+    def create_handlers(
+        cls,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        manager_store_triggers: Sequence[StoreTrigger],
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_config: "KVCacheConfig",
+        extra_config: Mapping[str, Any],
+    ) -> dict[StoreTrigger, StoreTriggerHandler]:
+        """Make one handler per store trigger, in trigger order.
+
+        The layout handlers come first, then one handler per trigger that the
+        manager asks for.
+
+        Args:
+            config: the offloading config of this engine.
+            manager_store_triggers: the triggers that the manager asks for.
+            events_tracker: the events tracker that the handlers will get.
+            vllm_config: the engine config.
+            kv_cache_config: the KV cache layout of this engine.
+            extra_config: kv_connector_extra_config of this connector.
+
+        Returns:
+            trigger -> handler instance.
+
+        Raises:
+            ValueError: on an empty or duplicate trigger set, or on a
+                trigger with no registered handler.
+
+        """
+        triggers = cls._get_store_triggers(config, manager_store_triggers)
+        handler_classes = [cls._get_handler_cls(trigger) for trigger in triggers]
+        for handler_cls in handler_classes:
+            handler_cls.check_support(
+                vllm_config, kv_cache_config, extra_config, events_tracker
+            )
+        return {
+            trigger: handler_cls(config, events_tracker)
+            for trigger, handler_cls in zip(triggers, handler_classes, strict=True)
+        }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _get_store_triggers(
+        cls,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        manager_store_triggers: Sequence[StoreTrigger],
+    ) -> tuple[StoreTrigger, ...]:
+        # The handlers that the KV cache layout requires run first.
+        layout_triggers: tuple[StoreTrigger, ...] = (
+            (StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF,) if config.supports_handoff else ()
+        )
+        triggers = layout_triggers + tuple(manager_store_triggers)

+                f"offloading manager must be unique and not empty: "
+                f"{triggers}"

+    def _get_handler_cls(cls, trigger: StoreTrigger) -> type[StoreTriggerHandler]:
+        handler_cls = cls._registry.get(trigger)
+        if handler_cls is None:

+        # req_id -> per group, the index of the next chunk to offer.
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs: dict[ReqId, list[int]] = {}
+
+    @override
+    def on_load_scheduled(
+        self,
+        req_status: RequestOffloadState,
+        num_cached_tokens: int,
+        load_chunk_ranges: Sequence[tuple[int, int]],
+        load_block_ids: Sequence[Sequence[int]],
+    ) -> None:
+        # Skip prefix-hit chunks for block-level policy; for
+        # request-level, the next stored chunk stays at 0 so all
+        # chunks (including hits) are offloaded.
+        if req_status.offloading_context.policy != OffloadPolicy.CHUNK_LEVEL:
+            return
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs[req_status.req.request_id] = [
+            cdiv(num_cached_tokens, group_config.tokens_per_chunk)
+            for group_config in self._config.kv_group_configs
+        ]
+
+    @override
+    def on_request_removed(self, req_id: ReqId) -> None:
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.pop(req_id, None)
+
+    @override
+    def on_request_restarted(self, req_id: ReqId) -> None:
+        # Offer every chunk again.
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.pop(req_id, None)
+
+    @override
+    def reset(self, req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState]) -> None:
+        # Active requests store again from chunk 0.
+        self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.clear()
+
+    @override
+    def first_live_chunk_idx(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, config_idx: int
+    ) -> int | None:
+        next_idxs = self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.get(req_status.req.request_id)
+        return 0 if next_idxs is None else next_idxs[config_idx]
+
+    def _next_idxs(self, req_status: RequestOffloadState) -> list[int]:
+        """The next chunk to offer in each group, created at 0."""
+        req_id = req_status.req.request_id
+        next_idxs = self._next_stored_chunk_idxs.get(req_id)
+        if next_idxs is None:
+            next_idxs = [0] * len(req_status.group_states)
+            self._next_stored_chunk_idxs[req_id] = next_idxs
+        return next_idxs
+
+    def _advance_stored_idx(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, num_offloadable_tokens: int
+    ) -> None:
+        # max(): at the prefill->decode transition of a chunk-aligned prompt,
+        # storable_chunks drops by one (the eagle exclusion kicks in), and the
+        # index must not move backwards past already-stored chunks.
+        apply_eagle_drop = not self._config.num_hash_lookahead_tokens
+        next_idxs = self._next_idxs(req_status)
+        for config_idx, (group_config, group_state) in enumerate(
+            zip(self._config.kv_group_configs, req_status.group_states)
+        ):
+            next_idxs[config_idx] = max(
+                next_idxs[config_idx],
+                req_status.storable_chunks(
+                    group_config,
+                    group_state,
+                    num_offloadable_tokens,
+                    apply_eagle_drop,
+                ),
+            )
+
+    @override
+    def build_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        blocks_per_chunk = self._config.blocks_per_chunk
+        for req_id in chain(
+            scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens,
+            scheduler_output.finished_req_ids or (),
+        ):
+            req_status = req_states.get(req_id)
+            if req_status is None:
+                continue
+            req = req_status.req
+            candidates = select_store_candidates(
+                self._config,
+                scheduler_output,
+                req_status,
+                self._next_idxs(req_status),
+            )
+            num_offloadable_tokens = candidates.num_offloadable_tokens
+            new_offload_keys = candidates.keys
+            group_store_ranges = candidates.group_ranges
+
+            if not new_offload_keys:
+                self._advance_stored_idx(req_status, num_offloadable_tokens)
+                continue
+
+            store_output = sink.prepare_store(new_offload_keys, req_status.req_context)
+            if store_output is None:
+                logger.warning("Request %s: cannot store chunks", req_id)
+                continue
+
+            if not store_output.keys_to_store:
+                self._advance_stored_idx(req_status, num_offloadable_tokens)
+                continue
+
+            ordered_keys_to_store = tuple(dict.fromkeys(store_output.keys_to_store))
+            keys_to_store = set(ordered_keys_to_store)
+
+            group_sizes: list[int] = []
+            block_indices: list[int] = []
+            src_block_ids: list[int] = []
+            fenced_block_ids: list[int] = []
+            deferred_fence_block_ids: list[int] = []
+            for group_config, group_state, store_range in zip(
+                self._config.kv_group_configs,
+                req_status.group_states,
+                group_store_ranges,
+            ):
+                is_sliding_window = (
+                    group_config.sliding_window_size_in_chunks is not None
+                )
+                start_chunk_idx, num_chunks = store_range
+                block_ids = group_state.block_ids
+                num_group_blocks = 0
+                start_gpu_block_idx: int | None = None
+                for idx, offload_key in enumerate(
+                    group_state.offload_keys[start_chunk_idx:num_chunks]
+                ):
+                    if offload_key not in keys_to_store:
+                        continue
+
+                    chunk_idx = start_chunk_idx + idx
+
+                    self._events_tracker.record_store(
+                        req, group_config, chunk_idx, offload_key
+                    )
+
+                    gpu_block_idx = chunk_idx * blocks_per_chunk
+                    if start_gpu_block_idx is None:
+                        start_gpu_block_idx = gpu_block_idx
+                    for i in range(blocks_per_chunk):
+                        block_id = block_ids[gpu_block_idx + i]
+                        # Keep null pages inside the chunk as placeholders so
+                        # later blocks retain their logical offsets in the CPU
+                        # chunk. The null GPU block is zeroed and can be copied
+                        # safely; it must not be fenced as a live allocation.
+                        src_block_ids.append(block_id)
+                        num_group_blocks += 1
+                        if block_id == 0:
+                            continue
+                        if is_sliding_window:
+                            fenced_block_ids.append(block_id)
+                        else:
+                            deferred_fence_block_ids.append(block_id)
+
+                group_sizes.append(num_group_blocks)
+                block_indices.append(start_gpu_block_idx or 0)
+
+            next_idxs = self._next_idxs(req_status)
+            for config_idx, (_, num_chunks) in enumerate(group_store_ranges):
+                next_idxs[config_idx] = max(next_idxs[config_idx], num_chunks)
+
+            # the non-sliding window blocks will be watched only
+            # when the request finishes
+            sink.add_job(
+                req_id,
+                ordered_keys_to_store,
+                GPULoadStoreSpec(
+                    src_block_ids,
+                    group_sizes=group_sizes,
+                    block_indices=block_indices,
+                ),
+                store_output.store_spec,
+                fenced_block_ids=fenced_block_ids or None,
+                deferred_fence_block_ids=deferred_fence_block_ids,
+            )

+from collections.abc import Mapping
+
+from typing_extensions import override
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.common import (
+    ReqId,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.events import (
+    OffloadingEventsTracker,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.state import (
+    RequestOffloadState,
+    SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.offloading.store_triggers.base import (  # noqa: E501
+    StoreJobSink,

+)

+class OnHandoffStoreHandler(StoreTriggerHandler):
+    """Stores the state blocks that the KV cache manager hands off
+    (StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF).
+
+    The hand-off arrives when a recurrent state block is about to be reused.
+    Its source is short-lived, so every store mode stores it at the same step.
+    """
+
+    trigger = StoreTrigger.ON_HANDOFF
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(config, events_tracker)
+        self._cow_source_groups = frozenset(
+            group_config.group_idx
+            for group_config in config.kv_group_configs
+            if group_config.requires_cow_source
+        )
+
+    @override
+    def first_live_chunk_idx(
+        self, req_status: RequestOffloadState, config_idx: int
+    ) -> int | None:
+        # The source blocks come from the scheduler output, not from the
+        # request's block list.
+        return None
+
+    @override
+    def build_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        block_state = scheduler_output.kv_connector_block_state
+        handoffs = block_state.boundary_state_offloads if block_state else None
+        if not handoffs:
+            return
+        self._build_aligned_boundary_store_jobs(handoffs, req_states, sink)
+        if self._config.supports_partial_tail:
+            self._build_partial_tail_store_jobs(
+                scheduler_output, handoffs, req_states, sink
+            )
+
+    def _build_aligned_boundary_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        handoffs: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]],
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        num_groups = len(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+        config_idx_by_group = {
+            config.group_idx: idx
+            for idx, config in enumerate(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+        }
+        for req_id, entries in handoffs.items():
+            req_status = req_states.get(req_id)
+            if req_status is None:
+                continue
+            req = req_status.req
+            max_boundary = req_status.num_offloadable_tokens(req.num_tokens)
+            for group_idx, block_id, boundary in entries:
+                config_idx = config_idx_by_group.get(group_idx)
+                if config_idx is None:
+                    continue
+                group_config = self._config.kv_group_configs[config_idx]
+                if (
+                    block_id == 0
+                    or boundary > max_boundary
+                    or boundary % group_config.tokens_per_chunk != 0
+                ):
+                    continue
+
+                key = req_status.register_boundary_key(group_idx, boundary)
+                store_output = sink.prepare_store([key], req_status.req_context)
+                if store_output is None:
+                    continue
+                if not store_output.keys_to_store:
+                    continue
+
+                group_sizes = [0] * num_groups
+                group_sizes[config_idx] = 1
+                block_indices = [0] * num_groups
+                block_indices[config_idx] = (
+                    boundary // group_config.tokens_per_block - 1
+                )
+                sink.add_job(
+                    req_id,
+                    [key],
+                    GPULoadStoreSpec(
+                        [block_id],
+                        group_sizes=group_sizes,
+                        block_indices=block_indices,
+                    ),
+                    store_output.store_spec,
+                    fenced_block_ids=[block_id],
+                )
+                self._events_tracker.record_store(
+                    req,
+                    group_config,
+                    boundary // group_config.tokens_per_chunk - 1,
+                    key,
+                )
+
+    def _build_partial_tail_store_jobs(
+        self,
+        scheduler_output: SchedulerOutput,
+        handoffs: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]],
+        req_states: Mapping[ReqId, RequestOffloadState],
+        sink: StoreJobSink,
+    ) -> None:
+        partial_tail_block_size = self._config.partial_tail_block_size
+        max_eagle_proof_margin = self._config.max_eagle_proof_margin
+        for req_id, entries in handoffs.items():
+            entries = [
+                entry for entry in entries if entry[2] % partial_tail_block_size != 0
+            ]
+            if not entries:
+                continue
+            req_status = req_states.get(req_id)
+            assert req_status is not None
+            if max_eagle_proof_margin and not req_status.loaded_from_offload:
+                # Requests that did not load from the offload tier keep their
+                # EAGLE tail in the GPU prefix cache; skip the store.
+                continue
+            boundaries = {boundary for _, _, boundary in entries}
+            assert len(boundaries) == 1
+            boundary = boundaries.pop()
+            req = req_status.req
+            group_states = {
+                group.group_idx: state
+                for group, state in zip(
+                    self._config.kv_group_configs, req_status.group_states
+                )
+            }
+            max_boundary = min(
+                req.num_prompt_tokens,
+                req_status.max_offload_tokens or req.num_prompt_tokens,
+            )
+            assert boundary > 0
+            assert boundary % self._config.tokens_per_hash == 0
+            assert boundary <= max_boundary
+
+            if max_eagle_proof_margin:
+                # The CoW hand-off arrives on the step that computes the prompt
+                # tokens past the boundary, and it is not offered again. Workers
+                # submit a store at the next step's start, after this step's
+                # forward, so count the prompt tokens this step computes.
+                prompt_tokens_after_step = min(
+                    req.num_computed_tokens
+                    + scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens.get(req_id, 0),
+                    req.num_prompt_tokens,
+                )
+                if boundary + max_eagle_proof_margin > prompt_tokens_after_step:
+                    # The EAGLE proof is not computed by the end of this step.
+                    continue
+
+            cow_blocks = {group_idx: block_id for group_idx, block_id, _ in entries}
+            assert self._cow_source_groups.issubset(cow_blocks)
+
+            assert boundary % partial_tail_block_size != 0
+            block_idx = boundary // partial_tail_block_size
+            if any(
+                group.group_idx not in self._cow_source_groups
+                and block_idx >= len(group_states[group.group_idx].block_ids)
+                for group in self._config.kv_group_configs
+            ):
+                continue
+            key_tokens = [
+                self._config.partial_tail_key_tokens(config_idx, boundary)
+                for config_idx in range(len(self._config.kv_group_configs))
+            ]
+            keys = [
+                req_status.register_boundary_key(group.group_idx, tokens)
+                for group, tokens in zip(self._config.kv_group_configs, key_tokens)
+            ]
+            block_ids = [
+                cow_blocks[group.group_idx]
+                if group.group_idx in self._cow_source_groups
+                else group_states[group.group_idx].block_ids[block_idx]
+                for group in self._config.kv_group_configs
+            ]
+            assert all(block_id != 0 for block_id in block_ids)
+
+            store_output = sink.prepare_store(keys, req_status.req_context)
+            if store_output is None:
+                continue
+            if not store_output.keys_to_store:
+                continue
+
+            for group_config, tokens, key in zip(
+                self._config.kv_group_configs, key_tokens, keys
+            ):
+                if key in store_output.keys_to_store:
+                    self._events_tracker.record_partial_store(
+                        req, group_config, tokens, key
+                    )
+
+            group_by_key = {key: idx for idx, key in enumerate(keys)}
+            accepted_groups = [group_by_key[key] for key in store_output.keys_to_store]
+            group_sizes = [0] * len(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+            block_indices = [0] * len(self._config.kv_group_configs)
+            for group_idx in accepted_groups:
+                group_sizes[group_idx] = 1
+                block_indices[group_idx] = block_idx
+            source_blocks = [block_ids[group_idx] for group_idx in accepted_groups]
+
+            sink.add_job(
+                req_id,
+                store_output.keys_to_store,
+                GPULoadStoreSpec(
+                    source_blocks,
+                    group_sizes=group_sizes,
+                    block_indices=block_indices,
+                ),
+                store_output.store_spec,
+                fenced_block_ids=source_blocks,
+            )

+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class GpuChunk:
+    """A group chunk to store when the block pool gives out one of its blocks."""
+
+    key: OffloadKey
+    config_idx: int
+    chunk_idx: int
+    # The GPU block ids of the chunk, without the null blocks.
+    block_ids: tuple[int, ...]
+    # The key of the data in each block of block_ids.
+    block_keys: tuple[OffloadKey, ...]
+    # The position of block_ids[0] inside the chunk.
+    start_idx: int
+
+
+class OverwriteMap:
+    """The group chunks on GPU blocks, to store before a block gets new data."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        # block_id -> the group chunks that hold the block
+        self.by_block: dict[int, list[GpuChunk]] = {}
+
+    def add(self, chunks: Iterable[GpuChunk]) -> None:
+        """Remember which chunks sit on each block."""
+        for chunk in chunks:
+            # A chunk with no non-null block has nothing to store.
+            if not chunk.block_ids:
+                continue
+            # A prefix hit offers the chunk of an existing entry again.
+            if chunk in self.by_block.get(chunk.block_ids[-1], ()):
+                continue
+            for block_id in chunk.block_ids:
+                self.by_block.setdefault(block_id, []).append(chunk)
+
+    def take_overwritten(
+        self, block_keys: dict[int, OffloadKey | None]
+    ) -> list[GpuChunk]:
+        """Remove and return the chunks whose blocks get different data.
+
+        block_keys maps a block id to the key that its new owner expects, or
+        to None for new data.
+        """
+        overwritten: list[GpuChunk] = []
+        for block_id, expected_key in block_keys.items():
+            for chunk in tuple(self.by_block.get(block_id, ())):
+                if chunk.block_keys[chunk.block_ids.index(block_id)] == expected_key:
+                    continue
+                for chunk_block_id in chunk.block_ids:
+                    chunks = self.by_block[chunk_block_id]
+                    chunks.remove(chunk)
+                    if not chunks:
+                        del self.by_block[chunk_block_id]
+                overwritten.append(chunk)
+        return overwritten
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        """Forget every chunk."""
+        self.by_block.clear()
+
+
+class OnOverwriteStoreHandler(StoreTriggerHandler):
+    """Offers a chunk when the block pool gives one of its blocks away
+    (StoreTrigger.ON_OVERWRITE)."""
+
+    trigger = StoreTrigger.ON_OVERWRITE
+
+    @classmethod
+    @override
+    def check_support(
+        cls,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        kv_cache_config: "KVCacheConfig",
+        extra_config: Mapping[str, Any],
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Refuse a config that an ON_OVERWRITE store cannot serve."""
+        if events_tracker.self_describing_enabled:
+            # A self-describing payload carries the tokens and the parent hash
+            # of the chunk, read from the request that stored it. The request
+            # of this store is usually finished by the time its block is
+            # reused, so the payload cannot be built.
+            raise ValueError(
+                "self_describing_kv_events is not supported with ON_OVERWRITE stores"
+            )
+        if vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner and kv_cache_config.needs_kv_cache_zeroing:
+            # The V2 model runner zeroes new blocks and applies the CoW copies
+            # in update_requests, before handle_preemptions flushes the
+            # ON_OVERWRITE jobs. Such a store would read zeroed or copied data
+            # and save it under a valid key.
+            raise ValueError(
+                "ON_OVERWRITE stores are not supported with the V2 model runner "
+                "when the KV cache needs zeroing (mixed-precision KV cache). "
+                "Set VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0."
+            )
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: SchedulerOffloadConfig,
+        events_tracker: OffloadingEventsTracker,
+    ):
+        super().__init__(config, events_tracker)
+        # A store waits until the data is about to be lost: the map holds the
+        # chunks that sit on GPU blocks, and a chunk is offered when one of
+        # its blocks gets different data.
+        self._overwrite_map = OverwriteMap()
+        # req_id -> per group, the first chunk not recorded in the map yet.
+        self._first_unrecorded_chunk_idxs: dict[ReqId, list[int]] = {}
+        # req_id -> the chunks of the scheduled load, added at its completion.
+        self._pending_loads: dict[ReqId, list[GpuChunk]] = {}
+        # block_id -> the key that the new owner expects in the block, or None
+        # for new data, for the blocks given out in this step. Rebuilt every
+        # step, in on_request_blocks_allocated and on_blocks_allocated.
+        self._allocated_block_keys: dict[int, OffloadKey | None] = {}
+
+    @override
+    def on_request_blocks_allocated(
+        self,
+        req_status: RequestOffloadState,
+        block_ids: Sequence[Sequence[int]],
+        start_block_idxs: Sequence[int],
+    ) -> None:
+        """Record the key that the new owner of each block expects."""
+        req = req_status.req
+        for group_config, group_block_ids, start in zip(
+            self._config.kv_group_configs, block_ids, start_block_idxs
+        ):
+            num_hashed_blocks = len(req.block_hashes) // group_config.hashes_per_block
+            for idx, bid in enumerate(group_block_ids, start):
+                # A null block holds nothing, and a block whose hash is not
+                # complete cannot be a prefix hit. on_blocks_allocated marks
+                # both as new data.
+                if bid != 0 and idx < num_hashed_blocks:
+                    self._allocated_block_keys[bid] = block_key(req, group_config, idx)
+
+    @override
+    def on_blocks_allocated(self, block_ids: Collection[int]) -> None:
+        """Mark the blocks of this step that no request claimed as new data."""
+        # A block of a group that is not offloaded, a block with no hash yet,
+        # or a copy destination gets new data. setdefault keeps the key that
